newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols weaken as spot travels old path.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols weaken as spot travels old path.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/pair options eroded as the spot retraced a well-worn groove and attention shifted to the dollar's downside potential.

Options analysts said risk reversals for one-month 25-delta dollar/yen options this morning were favoring yen calls, at flat/0.2, after the dollar veered toward 125.00 yen overnight on comments by Deputy U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers and worries about possible Bank of Japan intervention.

The shift in risk reversals toward yen calls and away from the yen put bias dominant over the past several months is consistent with the aggressive buying in short-dated yen calls seen earlier in the week, a trader for a U.S. investment bank said.
The trader said he was inclined to view dollar weakness as a pause in the longer-term uptrend and looked for the volatility curve to steepen in the meantime.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/yen options was 9.00/9.25 percent, compared with 9.10/9.30 for the previous session. One-year was about even at 10.15/10.35 percent.
With the dollar's grind higher depressing volatility, market participants have begun to focus on the currency's downside potential, said Alan Revercomb, options strategist for I.D.E.A. Inc.
"Upside enthusiasm has worn away," he said. "The downside could be more of a surprise."
Dollar/mark volatility also cooled, shedding 0.2 point, to 8.40/8.65 percent, in the one-month and about 0.1 point, to 9.10/9.30 percent, in the one-year.

Traders said getting past this morning's U.S. trade data with limited impact on the dollar allowed volatilities to ease. The trade deficit narrowed by 8.5 percent to $11.59 billion in February, while the gap with Japan fell by 0.9 percent to $4.26 billion.
By midday, the dollar had recovered much of its overnight losses and was hovering near 125.75 yen, pushing the risk reversal spread back to around par, traders said.
